chapter: Starting out in New York and Chicago
title: Mixed audiences and musicians' role in integration
summary: The Grand Terrace audience was mixed; Horace says musicians demanded to sit among audiences they entertained, helping break down segregation.

story.theme_name: Race and segregation in the jazz life
story.community_name: Segregation on the road and the bandstand

blocks.x: Now, again, was the audience at the Grant Terrace -- was that a white audience or --
Things were beginning to change there. (Inaudible) And I really -- I believe you'd agree with me 100 percent -- that the musicianship and the musicians had a lot to do with integration.
I do. You bet, cause there's one of the first places where it was happening.

Yes. We -- I say we, I mean you (unintelligible) and all of the great musicians -- we demanded that. If we were good enough to entertain you, we were good enough to sit among you and talk -- talk things over. And this is what gradually, I know, broke it down -- helped to break quite a bit of it. And I'm very happy now that we were instrumental -- we were a part of that.
